accepted.evidence: Turner explicitly gives Torwali aṣī́ eye under akṣi. Source æʂi retains the retroflex sibilant and final vowel, with its æ vowel preserved. Published phonetic notation, source locator and Bahrain dialect label are preserved.
Turner explicitly gives Torwali bāl hair under vāla. The source ba:l matches directly. Published phonetic notation, source locator and Bahrain dialect label are preserved.

Turner explicitly gives Torwali gām village under grāma. The p.52 source entry ga:m is distinct from the separate p.177 citation, which is not included in this image-check batch. Published phonetic notation, source locator and Bahrain dialect label are preserved.

Turner gives Torwali jīb tongue under jihvā. Source phonetic ji:b is rendered yīb by the existing IPA profile; that transcription-layer difference is preserved, not silently converted back to j. Published phonetic notation, source locator and Bahrain dialect label are preserved.

Turner gives Torwali dΛn tooth under danta. The source da:n has the same d-n skeleton with final t absent; its long vowel is retained. Published phonetic notation, source locator and Bahrain dialect label are preserved.

Turner section 2 explicitly gives Torwali dhimī smoke under dhūmikā, with *dhūmiyā/dhūmyā alternatives in the heading. The source dʰi:mi selects existing node6849-2 rather than dhūma section1; the alternative formation remains open. Published phonetic notation, source locator and Bahrain dialect label are preserved.

Turner section1 gives Torwali maǰ fish and neighbouring Pashai mās under matsya. The source ma:ʃ preserves its voiceless fricative and long vowel in this regional fish-family assignment; it is not the subsection *matsiya. Published phonetic notation, source locator and Bahrain dialect label are preserved.

Turner explicitly gives Torwali mās meat/flesh under māṃsa. The source ma:s is distinct from ma:ʃ fish on the same page; the separate sibilants and senses are preserved. Published phonetic notation, source locator and Bahrain dialect label are preserved.
Turner explicitly gives Torwali him snow under hima. The source hi:m preserves the long vowel as printed. Published phonetic notation, source locator and Bahrain dialect label are preserved.
